record.paper_title: Current Open Questions in Complete Mixability
record.original_question: For n > 3, can one fully characterize the set J_n(K) of n-tuples of distributions that are jointly mixable with joint center K, or equivalently the set M_n(μ) of distributions on ℝ that are n-completely mixable with center μ?

evidence.quote: For n = 1 or n = 2, the sets Jn(K) and Mn(μ) are fully characterized. For n > 3, a full characterization of either set is still an open question.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. For an integer $n\ge 1$, let $F_1,\dots,F_n$ be univariate cumulative distribution functions on $\mathbb{R}$. The tuple $(F_1,\dots,F_n)$ is called jointly mixable with center $K\in\mathbb{R}$ if there exist random variables $X_1,\dots,X_n$ defined on a common probability space, with $X_i\sim F_i$ for each $i$, such that
$$P(X_1+X_2+\cdots+X_n=K)=1.$$
Define
$$J_n(K)=\{(F_1,\dots,F_n): (F_1,\dots,F_n)\text{ is jointly mixable with center }K\}.$$
A distribution $F$ on $\mathbb{R}$ is called $n$-completely mixable with center $\mu$ if $(F,F,\dots,F)\in J_n(n\mu)$, and we set
$$M_n(\mu)=\{F: F\text{ is }n\text{-completely mixable with center }\mu\}.$$

Problem. For each integer $n>3$, give a full (necessary and sufficient) characterization of the set $J_n(K)$ of $n$-tuples of one-dimensional distributions that are jointly mixable with center $K$, or equivalently of the set $M_n(\mu)$ of distributions on $\mathbb{R}$ that are $n$-completely mixable with center $\mu$.
artifact.status_search_result: A full characterization of joint mixability and complete mixability for n ≥ 3 is widely cited as still open. Subsequent work (e.g., on elliptical distributions, distributions with monotone or unimodal-symmetric densities, and detection procedures) has produced sufficient conditions and partial results for special classes, but no general characterization for n > 3 has appeared in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Joint mixability of elliptical distributions and related families
status_evidence.snippet: Provides necessary and sufficient conditions for joint mixability within special classes (elliptical, monotone, unimodal-symmetric).
status_evidence.claim: Only special classes are characterized; the general case remains open.

status_evidence.title: Detecting complete and joint mixability
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces a Mixability Detection Procedure for cases not covered by theoretical results.
status_evidence.claim: General characterization is unavailable, motivating numerical detection.

status_evidence.title: Current open questions in complete mixability
status_evidence.snippet: For n = 1 or n = 2, J_n(K) and M_n(μ) are fully characterized; for n > 3 the full characterization is open.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly listed as open.
